chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Al-Hasan al-Zayyat, who said:

I entered upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) in a refurbished room. Then I returned to him the next day, and he was in a room in which there was nothing except a mat, and upon him was a coarse shirt. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The room which you saw was not my room. Rather, it is the room of the wife, and yesterday was her day.'

key_terms.يَوْمُهَا: her day (referring to the wife's turn in the Imam's household)

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith about the Imam's simple room and his wife's day teach about humility in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the asceticism (*zuhd*) of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) by contrasting his wife’s furnished room with his own sparse living space, which contained only a simple mat and a coarse shirt. It illustrates the practical application of modesty in domestic life, where the Imam’s personal quarters remained unadorned to reflect spiritual detachment, while accommodating his family’s comfort. This narrative serves as a key example in Shia scholarship for understanding the balance between worldly simplicity and familial responsibility.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Usman Bin Isa, from Abdullah Bin Muskan, from Al Hassan Al Zayyat who said,

‘I went over to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> in a refurbished room. Then I went again to him<sup>asws</sup> in the morning and he<sup>asws</sup> was in a room in which there was nothing except for a mat, and upon him<sup>asws</sup> was a coarse shirt. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This room which you saw was not my<sup>asws</sup> room. But rather is was a room of the wife, and yesterday was her day’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muskan from al- Hassan al-Zayyat who has said the following: “I once visited abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, in a well-furnished house; and the next day I visited him in a house where there was nothing except a mat. He (the Imam) wore a thick and rough-textured shirt. He (the Imam) said, ‘The house that you saw was not my house. It was the house of the woman and yesterday was her day.’”
